patch.description: Amazon registered Building A at 6000 TX-18 in Pecos County on August 4, 2026. The filing lists 189,060 square feet and an estimated USD 300 million construction cost. Its August–December 2026 construction window is a filed schedule; accessibility review completion does not establish an opening.
patch.longFormSummary:
Site and filed scope

  • Building A is registered at 6000 TX-18, Fort Stockton, Pecos County, Texas. Its accessibility filing lists 189,060 square feet. The record does not establish the previous use of the individual building footprint.

Construction and timeline

  • The filing lists August 1 to December 1, 2026 as the scheduled construction window. Completed accessibility review does not verify completed construction or an operational opening.

Cost

  • The Building A filing estimates USD 300 million for its own scope. This is a published filing estimate, not an allocation of the entire campus investment.

Campus imagery

  • Pacifico Energy supplies the shared GW Ranch campus renderings. These illustrate the overall campus and do not identify Building A or prove that it is complete. The developer page does not establish public reaction to this individual filing.

patch.description: Al Shuaibah 1 is a 600 MW solar photovoltaic plant in Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia. ACWA’s prospectus records commercial operation in November 2024. Its individual construction budget is not separately allocated from the two-plant programme.
patch.longFormSummary:
Plant and programme

  • Al Shuaibah 1 is a solar photovoltaic plant in Makkah Province, Saudi Arabia. Its 600 MW plant rating is separate from the combined two-plant programme.

Operation and timeline

  • ACWA’s 2025 prospectus records commercial operation in November 2024. The month is the stated precision, not a verified exact opening day.

Cost and ownership

  • The plants are jointly owned through ACWA Power, Badeel and SAPCO. The combined financing announcement does not publish a plant-specific construction budget; no share of that programme total is assigned here.

Public reaction

  • The owner welcomed the financing milestone as progress toward Saudi renewable-energy goals. This is an attributed programme reaction shared by both plants, not an independent assessment of this plant’s operation.

patch.longFormSummary:
Site and development

  • Amazon announced a third northwest Louisiana data-center campus at Resilient Technology Park in Shreveport on August 18, 2026. STACK Infrastructure is the developer and owner; the campus supports cloud computing and AI.

Investment and jobs

  • The additional campus has USD 6 billion of planned investment and 210 expected direct new jobs. The USD 18 billion investment and 750 direct jobs describe all three regional campuses, not this site alone.

Construction and delivery

  • KSLA’s August 18 report gives a first-building completion target in 2027 and a full-project buildout of three to five years. These are reported targets, not completed milestones.

Infrastructure and public process

  • Amazon says it will fund the infrastructure required by its operations. The up-to-USD 400 million water investment covers all three campuses and is not a separate Resilient construction budget.
  • Caddo officials sought water safeguards and environmental impact studies in June. Commissioner John Atkins supported development while calling for impact studies; those requests do not establish that all permits or appeals have been completed.

patch.title: Triboro Commerce Park: Seven-Building Proposal Withdrawn
patch.description: Triboro Commerce Park proposed seven data centers in Olyphant on a property of more than 400 acres. The borough engineer confirmed that those plans had been withdrawn in a June 10, 2026 report. The actual withdrawal day is unpublished. ERCOR Triboro’s separate proposal is covered by its own pin.
patch.longFormSummary:
Site and distinct proposals

  • Triboro Commerce Park’s withdrawn seven-building proposal and Sansone Group’s ERCOR Triboro proposal are separate projects. The June 10 report describes the commerce park’s property as more than 400 acres and ERCOR’s purchase as 500 acres.

Withdrawal and zoning

  • The borough engineer confirmed withdrawal of the commerce park’s seven-building plans in the June 10 report. The underlying withdrawal date is unpublished. The June 9 zoning settlement regulated data-center uses; it did not approve construction.

Cost and public response

  • No project-specific construction budget or electrical capacity is established by these reports. The USD 80 million land transaction is not construction cost.
  • Residents opposed data-center expansion at the June 9 council meeting. The accompanying photographs show that meeting and shared zoning debate; they are not project renderings or proof of construction.

patch.title: ERCOR Triboro: Seven Data Centers Proposed in Olyphant
patch.description: ERCOR Triboro, a Sansone Group company, proposed a data-center campus in Olyphant. A June 26, 2026 report describes seven two-story buildings and a substation across nearly 471 acres, revising an earlier nine-building account. ERCOR sued to bypass conditional-use hearings; the report does not establish a final court outcome or construction approval.
patch.longFormSummary:
Site and distinct proposals

  • Triboro Commerce Park’s withdrawn seven-building proposal and Sansone Group’s ERCOR Triboro proposal are separate projects. The June 10 report describes the commerce park’s property as more than 400 acres and ERCOR’s purchase as 500 acres.

Revised layout and legal process

  • The June 26 report describes seven two-story buildings, each with a 204,500-square-foot footprint, and a substation across nearly 471 acres. This later layout replaces the nine-building account in the June 10 report; footprint and total floor area are distinct.
  • ERCOR sued to obtain a zoning permit without conditional-use hearings, arguing that earlier warehouse approvals protected its application. That is the developer’s legal argument, not a verified court ruling approving data-center construction.

Cost and public response

  • No project-specific construction budget or electrical capacity is established by these reports. The USD 80 million land transaction is not construction cost.
  • Residents opposed data-center expansion at the June 9 council meeting. The accompanying photographs show that meeting and shared zoning debate; they are not project renderings or proof of construction.

patch.title: SpaceX Starbase Louisiana: USD 100 Billion Spaceport Announced
patch.description: SpaceX and Louisiana announced a planned USD 100 billion spaceport in Vermilion Parish on August 25, 2026. The state describes five launch complexes with two pads each and 3,000 expected direct jobs over ten years. Construction is targeted for 2027 and a first launch as early as 2029. These are planned milestones; residents are challenging the public process around the parish deal.
patch.longFormSummary:
Announced project and location

  • Louisiana’s August 25, 2026 announcement confirms a planned SpaceX launch facility in Vermilion Parish near Pecan Island. The project uses former Exxon property. SpaceX’s acquisition counsel separately reports approximately 130,000 acres acquired; that transaction area is not a surveyed construction footprint.

Planned investment and scope

  • The state announcement reports USD 100 billion of planned investment and 3,000 direct jobs over ten years. Full buildout is planned to include five launch complexes with two launch pads each, propellant production, power generation, vehicle processing and employee housing.

Construction and launch targets

  • Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with the first launch targeted as early as 2029. Those targets establish neither current physical construction nor completion of the entire spaceport.

Approval and public concerns

  • October 26 reporting describes residents’ litigation alleging violations of open-meetings requirements around the parish’s deal. The litigation is an unresolved public-process issue, not a finding that the whole project is cancelled.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: August 25, 2026 is the confirmed state announcement date. Construction in 2027 and a first launch as early as 2029 remain targets, not completed work.

patch.title: Yellow Pine Solar III: 100 MW Solar and 225 MW Storage Filing
patch.description: Yellow Pine Solar III LLC’s 2026 Nevada application describes 100 MWac of solar and 225 MW of co-located storage on 1,008.94 acres in Clark County. The application targets construction in Q2 2026 and commercial operation in Q2 2027. Nevada approved its tax-abatement application on June 3; this does not confirm physical construction. Conflicting investment scopes remain under review.
patch.longFormSummary:
Phase-specific filing

  • Yellow Pine Solar III LLC’s 2026 Nevada application describes a 100 MWac solar facility co-located with 225 MW of battery storage in Clark County. The site is 1,008.94 acres at 6901 Tecopa Road. Solar generation and storage power are separate ratings; no storage duration is inferred.

Schedule and regulatory process

  • The application anticipates construction beginning in Q2 2026 and commercial operation in Q2 2027. The June 3 tax-abatement hearing does not verify that physical construction has started or that the facility is operational.
  • Nevada’s June 3 hearing minutes identify this application as AFN 26-0401SPV and record approval of the partial tax-abatement application. No public comments were made at either public-comment period.

Cost conflict

  • The application lists USD 583.6 million total capital investment, with 25% expended in Nevada. The hearing minutes instead record approximately USD 149.9 million investment in the facility. These are not treated as interchangeable construction budgets; price remains unpublished pending reconciliation of the scope and final agreement.
  • The state index’s link labelled Legal Order opens a Libra Solar order rather than a Yellow Pine III order. The wrong-project document is excluded from this profile.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: The 2026 application targets Q2 2027 commercial operation. June 30 is a quarter anchor, not an announced exact opening day.

patch.longFormSummary:
Stonebridge Associates proposed a 16-building campus on the 569-acre Powder Mills site across North Beaver and Mahoning townships. A July 2026 report attributed an investment of more than USD 15 billion to the developer.

The reported proposal does not establish IT-load capacity, construction commencement or final municipal approval. The current approval and appeal position requires a dated municipal or court decision.

September zoning and appeal record

  • Mahoning Township’s September 3 notice identifies SS Penn LLC’s appeal of the June 4 zoning letter for Powder Mill Works property at 3478 Howard Drive and 152 McClelland Road, and schedules a September 15 hearing. The notice does not report the outcome.
  • WKBN reporting republished by AOL on September 11 says North Beaver Township’s board unanimously denied Stonebridge Associates’ appeal. This is a reported appeal decision, not voluntary withdrawal or proof of construction. The dated written decisions, any later court appeal and the Mahoning outcome remain unverified.
